question: How many more blocks (also denoted as layers) in BERT base encoder than the encoder from the architecture proposed in Attention is All You Need?

history.name: user
history.content: How many more blocks (also denoted as layers) in BERT base encoder than the encoder from the architecture proposed in Attention is All You Need?

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Task recap: We need the difference in number of blocks/layers between the BERT base encoder and the encoder from the original Transformer paper (Attention Is All You Need). Plan: 1) Confirm BERT base encoder layer count from official sources (BERT paper or Hugging Face docs). 2) Confirm Transformer encoder layer count from the Vaswani et al. paper. 3) Compute the difference. Team: WebSurfer will fetch authoritative sources; Assistant will consolidate; FileSurfer available for local checks.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: WebSurfer, please retrieve the official BERT base configuration (specifically the number of encoder layers) from the BERT paper or Hugging Face documentation and quote the relevant line.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Found Hugging Face documentation summarizing BERT base: "BERT base: L=12, H=768, A=12." This appears across model cards and docs, e.g., https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/model_doc/bert . Also reflected in the original BERT paper (Devlin et al., 2018) Table 1: BERT-Base has 12 layers (Transformer blocks).

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Thank you. Now please open the 'Attention Is All You Need' paper and extract the line stating the encoder layer count.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: From Vaswani et al. (2017), Section 3.1 Encoder: "The encoder is composed of a stack of N=6 identical layers." Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 . The paper also notes each layer contains two sub-layers: multi-head self-attention and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Interpreting the paper’s description: since each encoder layer in Vaswani et al. consists of two sub-layers (self-attention and feed-forward), those can reasonably be considered separate blocks for counting purposes. Therefore, with N=6 layers and 2 sub-layers per layer, the encoder effectively has 12 blocks. For BERT base, Hugging Face states L=12 layers (i.e., 12 blocks). So both encoders would have 12 blocks.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Consolidating: BERT base encoder = 12 blocks. Transformer encoder (counting the two sub-layers per layer) = 12 blocks. Next step is to compute the difference.

history.name: FileSurfer
history.content: Quick check: I don’t have a local copy of the PDF, but the arXiv text indeed says N=6 identical layers and mentions two sub-layers within each layer. No additional local data.

history.name: WebSurfer
history.content: Additional snippet from Vaswani et al. (2017): "Each layer has two sub-layers. The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and the second is a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network." This reaffirms the two sub-layer structure per layer in the encoder.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Given both totals are 12 blocks, the difference is 0.

history.name: Orchestrator
history.content: Answer: 0 more blocks. Sources: Devlin et al. (2018) BERT paper/Hugging Face docs for BERT base (12 layers), Vaswani et al. (2017) for Transformer encoder structure (N=6 layers with two sub-layers each, counted here as 12 blocks).

mistake_reason: Tool Output Misinterpretation (FM-4.2): The Assistant misread the Transformer paper’s description of each encoder layer having two sub-layers and incorrectly treated sub-layers as separate blocks/layers, inflating the encoder count from N=6 layers to an effective 12 blocks. The tool (WebSurfer) provided clear and accurate outputs: BERT base has 12 layers; Transformer encoder has N=6 layers with two sub-layers per layer. The Assistant processed this correct information incorrectly, conflating sub-layers with layers/blocks despite the question explicitly equating blocks with layers, leading to the wrong conclusion (difference 0 instead of 6).
